Nikhil / Ben — thanks for the ping. I reviewed Stunbridge's redline and suggest the following approach (high level):

1) Role clarification (Controller/Processor)
- We can accept Controller/Processor split but need two explicit additions in the DPA: (a) a list of Customer responsibilities (data subject requests, lawful basis) and (b) a Processor obligations section referencing our security practices.
- Keep the objection flow to 30 days but add a \"reasonable security or compliance-based objection\" carveout so we don't have to refuse broad categories without remediation suggestions.

2) SCCs annex and transfer-impact addendum
- Accept inclusion of EU SCCs (2021) as an annex. We'll add a sentence tying SCCs to the DPA and clarifying precedence (DPA controls where specific).
- We should add a transfer-impact addendum that enumerates subprocessor tiers and a fallback routing policy (if EU KMS unavailable, keys remain in EU via customer-managed KMS or Private deployment).

3) KMS / Key custody language
- We cannot universally guarantee Redwood-managed KMS keys will reside in the EU in Hosted mode. Options to offer: (i) Private deployment with EU HSM (recommended for regulated customers), (ii) Customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) with documented instructions, (iii) Dedicated with geo pinning as a limited commitment (needs infra SOW).
- I'll draft three short clauses and a table of options to include in the order form so procurement can select.

4) Export/Controls and pricing
- Add a new export-controls clause limiting outbound transfers and referencing sanctions screening. For pricing impact: Ben, we'll need a back-of-envelope surcharge for EU KMS dedicated or Private deployment (engineering ops + HSM costs).

I'll attach a redline with tracked legal edits (see nik_dpa_comments_v1.docx). Please review and flag anything that is a commercial decision vs. legal.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Quick infra/commercial notes:

- EU KMS: Engineering confirms we can support customer-managed KMS in EU in ~4 weeks (docs + onboarding) and Private deployment with EU HSM in ~8-10 weeks (project SOW). Dedicated with geo-pin is possible but requires a 12-week lead and a minimum capacity commit.
- Surcharge estimates: Customer-managed KMS — $0 (self-managed) + onboarding fee ~$6k. Private (EU HSM) — estimated setup $28k + monthly infra premium ~$3k. Dedicated geo-pin — depends on committed GPUs; estimate needed per-order.
- Order form approach: include a short checklist row in the order form that selects KMS option: Hosted (no guarantee), BYOK (customer-managed), Private (EU HSM) — each with a pricing cell. That keeps commercial clarity and avoids legal commits we can't meet.

I've annotated the redline with pricing placeholders. Laura — if legal can review the final fallback sentence for EU KMS (we propose: \"If Redwood cannot provide EU-hosted managed KMS under the Hosted offering, customer may elect BYOK or Private deployment with the associated fees and timelines documented in the Order Form\"), we can move forward.

Ben Carter
